text: git check-ignore (even -q) exits 0 for a path whose last matching rule is a ! re-include, so it reports every re-included .gitkeep as ignored. The honest reading of a gitignore negation is: git ls-files --others --exclude-standard lists it (tracked-able) vs --ignored does not.
memory.js selftest hard-codes three coupled totals (world-note count, cache-entry count, FORGOT count); every added remember/recall check shifts all three — recount them together.

loop.js: a plan's 'as' must be applied before AS is read, and a resume must never inherit the first run's --approve for an act cut mid-flight — otherwise a kill -9 between act-start and record replays an outward side effect on old consent.
